description.extended:
Russ Meyer's three-volume autobiography, self-published in 2000 after more than ten years of work, tells the filmmaker's life in the third person under the pen name Adolph Albion Schwartz, with more than 2,400 duotone photographs from his archive.

Volumes one and two carry the life story. It runs from a California childhood through service as a combat cameraman with the 166th Signal Photo Company in Europe, then postwar glamour work and early Playboy centerfolds, then the films and marriages. Volume three is a filmography. Each picture is retold through sequential frame enlargements and stills, with a chapter on the unfinished Sex Pistols film Who Killed Bambi? The set runs to 1,213 pages on heavy stock with sewn signatures. Each volume is bound in blue cloth lettered in gilt and issued without a jacket under Meyer's own Hauck Publishing imprint in Hollywood.

Meyer (1922-2004) directed The Immoral Mr. Teas (1959), Faster, Pussycat! Kill! Kill! (1965), Vixen! (1968) and Beyond the Valley of the Dolls (1970). Before the films he worked as a still photographer on Hollywood productions and shot three early Playboy centerfolds, one of his wife Eve Meyer. The library holds all three volumes.
description.artist_bio: Russ Meyer (1922-2004), American filmmaker and photographer. Combat cameraman with the 166th Signal Photo Company in the Second World War; postwar still photographer on Hollywood productions and glamour photographer who shot three early Playboy centerfolds. Directed The Immoral Mr. Teas (1959), Faster, Pussycat! Kill! Kill! (1965), Vixen! (1968), Beyond the Valley of the Dolls (1970), Supervixens (1975) and Beneath the Valley of the Ultra-Vixens (1979).

Pagination 359 + 418 + 436 pp. Two ISBNs circulate for the set, 9780962179723 (recorded) and 9780962179709.
